question.value: What are the spatially resolved molecular gas, dust and star-formation properties of the lensed SMG SDP.81 at z=3.042, and how are its gas, dust and stellar components arranged in the source plane?

evidence.quote: We present spatially-resolved properties of molecular gas and dust in a gravitationally-lensed submillimeter galaxy H-ATLAS J090311.6$+$003906 (SDP.81) at $z=3.042$ revealed by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00016.SV.

results_numeric.quantity: Number of molecular clumps in CO(5–4)

evidence.quote: We identified 14 molecular clumps in the CO(5–4) line data.
The SFR density ranges between 100–300 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ kpc$^{-2}$
with a gas depletion time scale of $\sim$100 Myr
A velocity gradient with a peak-to-peak value of $\sim$300 km s$^{-1}$ in the north-south direction can be seen
The molecular and dust clumps are confined within a $\sim$2 kpc region, while the spatial extent of the stellar components is as large as $\sim$6 kpc and offset toward the west.
the spatial extent of the stellar components is as large as $\sim$6 kpc and offset toward the west.
the brighter component of the foreground lens galaxy has the Sérsic index of $n=4.42$ (elliptical), while the fainter component has the index of $n=1.03$ (exponential).
The rms error to the fit is 0.085$''$ in right ascension and 0.100$''$ in declination.

results_numeric.quantity: Offset between SDSS lens and ALMA continuum

evidence.quote: match the coordinates of the continuum emission detected in Band 4, 6, and 7 (cite: alma15b) within 0.015$''$.

findings_qualitative.value: Clump surface densities exceed local spirals by >3 orders of magnitude and lie on the burst sequence

evidence.quote: The surface density of molecular gas ($\Sigma_{\rm H_2}$) and star-formation rate ($\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$) of the clumps are more than three orders of magnitude higher than those found in local spiral galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: Sigma_SFR/Sigma_H2 ratios consistent with Milky Way clumps

evidence.quote: the derived $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}/\Sigma_{\rm H_2}$ ratios are consistent with the values found in the Milky Way clumps
We found that some of the clumps do not appear to be extended in the transverse direction, and it is likely that they are unresolved.

findings_qualitative.value: Gas surface density appears higher in centre of disk

evidence.quote: The molecular gas surface density appears to be higher in the central part of the molecular/dust

claims.hypothesis: z~3 molecular clumps follow the local starburst star-formation law
claims.experiment: Derive Sigma_H2 and Sigma_SFR per clump from CO(5–4) and 1.0 mm continuum
claims.result: Clumps lie on burst sequence with ~100 Myr depletion time (normal sequence if Galactic alpha_CO)
claims.finding: Star-formation law applies to z~3 clumps

evidence.quote: suggesting that $z \sim 3$ molecular clumps follow the star-formation law derived for local starburst galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas forms a rotating disk
claims.experiment: Source-plane mapping of clump mean velocities
claims.finding: May indicate a rotating gas disk

evidence.quote: The molecular clumps have a systematic velocity gradient in the north-south direction, which may indicate a rotating gas disk.

claims.experiment: Source-plane positions of clumps and HST stellar points via lens model
claims.result: Gas/dust within ~2 kpc; stars over ~6 kpc offset west
claims.finding: Either obscured rotating disk or merger with tidal features

evidence.quote: Alternatively, SDP.81 can be explained by a merging system, where dusty starbursts occur in the region where the two galaxies collide, surrounded by tidal features traced in the stellar components.

why_this_data.value: Lensing plus long-baseline ALMA gives ~200 pc resolution

evidence.quote: offering an excellent opportunity to study the spatially-resolved properties of an SMG.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Galactic alpha_CO = 4.3 moves clumps to normal sequence

evidence.quote: these clumps are located on the sequence of normal star-forming galaxies.
Alternatively, SDP.81 may be a merging system, where dusty starbursts occur in the interface between the two colliding galaxies while the tidal features are widely extended.

limitations_admitted.value: Multiple images hard to identify due to low S/N

evidence.quote: because of the low SN, it may be difficult to identify all of the multiples in the CO(5–4) image.

limitations_admitted.value: Filling factor may be below unity

evidence.quote: Note that if the filling factor is less than unity, the data points in Figure [1](#fig:sk) will shift to the upper-right direction.

limitations_admitted.value: CO(5–4) may not trace whole disk

evidence.quote: The CO(5–4) line we used in this study has a relatively high critical density ($10^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$) and it may not trace the gas of the entire disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial extent of stellar components not considered

evidence.quote: the spatial extent of each component is not taken into account.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single integrated T_dust applied to all clumps ignores temperature gradients
Fixed CO(5–4)/CO(1–0)=0.3 and alpha_CO dominate surface density systematics
Clump detection at low S/N with low thresholds may include spurious clumps
Velocity gradient based on few clumps without kinematic modelling
